text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's parliament approved the resignation of Prime Minister Zhan Videnov with 211 votes, three voted against and nine abstained.

-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet is expected to raise electricity prices from January 1 under its scheme of their monthly revision in line with inflation and the lev/dollar exchange rate, Energy minister Roumen Ovcharov said. @

-- The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said it had extended another 24 billion levs to the Finance Ministry from a total of 115 billion lev direct loan to the government under the 1996 budget revisison. On Friday the BNB extended the first tranche of 55 billion levs.

-- Possible street rallies organised by Bulgaria's biggest opposition Union of Democratic Forces will not influence the nomination of a new government by the ruling Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP), the BSP leader Georgi Parvanov said. @
-- Another four people have been found frozen to death in snow storms in Bulgaria, bringing the death toll to 12 since December 24.

-- The price of central heating in Bulgaria should be raised to the lev equivalent of $20 per gigacalorie in 1997 from 3,945 levs ($8) now to prevent further losses of central heating firms, Energy Minister Roumen Ovcharov said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
